newsitem.title: JAPAN: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA UNDER PRESSURE IN GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-TOMBA UNDER PRESSURE IN GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Alberto Tomba's reputation for performing best when the stakes are highest will be put to the test this weekend when the Italian ski ace attempts to ensure his own survival as a World Cup giant slalom racer.

The flamboyant veteran from Bologna, who has yet to place in a giant slalom race this season, risks missing the World Cup giant slalom final in Vail, Colorado, next week unless he can pull off a strong finish in Saturday's event on Mount Higashidate in the central Japan Alps.
The top 25 skiers in each discipline automatically qualify for the Vail finals.

But even should he fail to do really well in the giant slalom he could still qualify for the Vail race by topping 400 overall World Cup points. He currently has 292, all earned in the slalom in which he is ranked fourth, and therefore a further 108 from the two events this weekend would be enough.
He also needs 400 overall points by the end of the season in order to start in giant slalom events next season.
Tomba will have two chances this weekend to boost his overall total, the giant slalom on Saturday and Sunday's slalom on nearby Mount Yakebitai plus the slalom world final in Vail.

After missing races before Christmas because of injury, Tomba crashed out of a giant slalom at Kranjska Gora, Slovenia, in January, and skied off the course at the world championships in Sestriere, Italy, last month.
For the first time in a decade, Tomba was pushed out of the top 15 seeds in giant slalom.

Tomba, double Olympic gold medallist and five-time world champion in the event, has never won a World Cup race in Japan, but hopes to change that when he starts 20th on the course which will host the event at next year's Nagano Olympics.
Swiss Michael von Gruenigen, reigning world giant slalom champion, holds a solid 159-point lead in the discipline over Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway.
Aamodt, second to speed specialist Luc Alphand in the overall standings, would need to win both events this weekend in order to overtake the Frenchman before the World Cup finals in Vail.

Aamodt's team mate Lasse Kjus, defending World Cup overall champion, won the last downhill before the Vail finals last week in Kvitfjell, Norway, and is aiming for a giant slalom win after taking the runner-up spot in the world championships last month.
Kjus's hopes of defending his overall title were dampened when a bad case of flu forced him to miss a month of World Cup racing at the end of December and early January.
Josef Strobl of Austria, fourth-ranked in the overall standings, will be looking for another victory after winning a super-G event in Kvitfjell last week.

Training was held early Friday morning before the unseasonably warm weather at this resort 60 kms northeast of Nagano had softened the course. Temperatures are expected to drop below freezing overnight.
